name: AISLE
one_line: AISLE's platform of AI agents that finds vulnerabilities in source code, triages them, writes and tests patches, and delivers them as pull requests for people to merge.
note: Everything here is from public pages. Facts carry their source and the time they were read; the hypothesis and the suggestions are ours and say so. GAMMA-Ray is a beta standard: every rating is experimental.

gamma_ray.built_from: AISLE's own public product, blog and about pages, and third-party vulnerability records (OpenSSL, curl, Samba) that credit its work

configs.what: The platform connected to a customer's repositories, delivering findings and patches as pull requests.
The customer sets, per severity and repository, that AISLE goes on from triage to open a pull request with a tested patch.
A customer connects AISLE's read-only MCP server to its own coding agent.

facts.label: It works across several domains or systems
facts.fact: The platform page states it plugs into the customer's scanners, repositories and CI.
facts.quote: AISLE plugs into the scanners, repos, and CI you already run

facts.label: The agent works independently; the person approves critical decisions only
facts.fact: The page states AISLE writes and tests a patch and opens a pull request, that the customer decides per severity and repository how far it goes, and that a person on the customer's team merges; no default is stated.
facts.quote: Nothing reaches your main branch until someone on your team merges it.

facts.label: It connects to external tools or services across a trust boundary
facts.fact: AISLE connects from its own service to the customer's hosted version control systems.
facts.quote: AISLE connects to GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps.

facts.label: High-impact actions need a person's approval
facts.fact: A merge to the main branch needs a person on the customer's team; AISLE opens the pull request and waits.
facts.quote: it opens the pull request and waits for human approval

facts.label: Its limits and known failure cases are documented for those who use it
facts.fact: The page states which findings get guidance instead of a patch, and that a fix breaking tests goes back to the team.
facts.quote: When findings can't be safely patched, it provides clear remediation advice instead.

facts.label: The data it uses is described
facts.fact: The privacy policy lists customer data as code repositories and related data submitted to the service.
facts.quote: Code repositories and related data submitted to Services

help.label: Our hypothesis, not their claim. Built from public pages only; nothing of theirs was tested.
help.pitch: RiskMandate would measure, for one real deployment of AISLE's agents, what each agent was asked to do (its mandate), what its credentials and connections actually let it reach (its grant), and the difference between the two (the gap), and keep that as a written record. It is read-only: never in the request path.
